title: Product Price Risk and Liquidity Management: Evidence from the Electricity Industry
authors: Chen Lin; Thomas M Schmid; Michael S. Weisbach
near_miss_reason: Not a near-miss: no main-text column estimates the binary market-introduction indicator with unit and calendar-time FE. Table 5 columns 1-2 regress cash on d_market_l in a pre/post collapse with at most two rows per firm and no time index, absorbing firm FE only (column 2 adds firm covariates: size, cash flow, leverage, lagged log GDP per capita); Table 5 columns 3-4 replace the indicator with the continuous volatility measure vola_weighted_zero_noln (zero before market introduction) with firm, year and quarter(-by-country) FE and the same covariates. Electricity wholesale-market introductions are staggered across countries (28 distinct first quarters for 125 switching firms in data_marketintro.dta, never-market firms present), but the main design (Tables 2-4) uses continuous price volatility and IV.
eligible_reason: Not a staggered binary TWFE design as reported. Main design (Tables 2-4) regresses firm cash holdings on continuous log electricity-price volatility with firm covariates and firm, year, country x quarter FE, plus an IV (weather volatility, ivreghdfe). The only binary staggered treatment (market introduction, Table 5) is estimated without calendar-time FE on a collapsed pre/post sample, or as a continuous volatility variable with covariates. No qualifying specification.
design_notes: Stata (reghdfe, ivreghdfe). Firm-quarter panel of electricity producers in 35 countries (data_world.dta, 5,784 obs, 213 firms) and a US-only panel (data_usonly.dta). Treatment is continuous (log volatility of wholesale electricity prices, log weather volatility as instrument, log demand-forecast volatility). Table 5 market introduction tests: collapsed pre/post firm data with firm FE only (cols 1-2) and firm-quarter panel with volatility set to zero before market introduction (cols 3-4, 11,360 obs, 336 firms, 52 countries).
